name: Kingdom in the Clouds: The Andes Before and After the Inca
description: Potatoes, llamas and knotted cords, the empire Pachacuti built, the conquest that seized it, the silver that flowed from it, and the revolts and wars that ended Spanish rule.

checkpoints.name: Gifts of the mountains
checkpoints.note: In the Andes of South America, farmers tame the potato and herders the llama. Cacao is already used in what is now Ecuador. Knotted quipu cords appear by about 2500 BCE, and on the southern coast of Peru the Nazca people begin scraping giant lines and figures into the desert.

checkpoints.name: Before the empire
checkpoints.note: Inca legend says their first ruler came out of Lake Titicaca. By about 1100 the Inca are settled at Cusco in a high valley, worshipping the sun and their ancestors in the Inca religion. Pachacuti, the ruler who will make them an empire, is born in 1391.

checkpoints.name: The four quarters
checkpoints.note: From 1438 Pachacuti turns the Inca Empire into the largest state in the Americas and rebuilds Cusco in stone. Machu Picchu rises on a ridge, the Inca road system runs the length of the Andes, and officials keep accounts on quipus. Smallpox arrives ahead of the Spanish, and a civil war leaves Atahualpa on the throne.

checkpoints.name: Conquest
checkpoints.note: Francisco Pizarro seizes Atahualpa at Cajamarca in 1532, takes a vast ransom and kills him in 1533. The Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire follows. Pizarro founds Lima in 1535, the Viceroyalty of Peru is set up in 1542, priests write down Quechua, and the last Inca stronghold falls in 1572.

checkpoints.name: Silver and revolt
checkpoints.note: Andean silver is minted into Spanish dollars, feeding the price revolution in Europe. Through the Columbian exchange the potato feeds the Old World, and quinine from Andean bark is used against malaria. Tupac Amaru II leads a great revolt in 1780 and is executed in 1781, and Alexander von Humboldt studies the Andes.

checkpoints.name: Independence
checkpoints.note: Jose de San Martin proclaims the independence of Peru in 1821, and in 1824 Antonio Jose de Sucre wins the battle that ends the Viceroyalty of Peru. In 1845 potato blight brings famine to Ireland, showing how far the Andean potato has come to feed Europe.
